title: The ideal sheaf of a base-changed closed immersion
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_Z\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $g:X'\to X$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. The projection $i':Z'=Z\times_XX'\to X'$ from the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] is a closed immersion, with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_{Z'}=\operatorname{im}(g^*\mathcal I_Z\to\mathcal O_{X'})$, where $g^*$ denotes module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] and the arrow is induced by $\mathcal I_Z\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_X$. If $g$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], this arrow is injective, so it identifies $g^*\mathcal I_Z$ with $\mathcal I_{Z'}$. In particular, if $X$ is a scheme over a field $k$, $x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ is a closed immersion and $K/k$ is a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], then for $X_K=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $x_K=\operatorname{Spec}K\to X_K$ [def-pc-base-change], the canonical map identifies $\mathcal I_{x_K}$ with $g^*\mathcal I_x$, where $g:X_K\to X$ is the projection.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], $i'$ is a closed immersion. To compute its ideal, cover $X$ by affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$; by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] and [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], $Z\times_XU=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ with $I=\mathcal I_Z(U)$. Cover $g^{-1}(U)$ by affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $Z'\times_{X'}V=\operatorname{Spec}((A/I)\otimes_AB)=\operatorname{Spec}(B/IB)$, so the ideal of $i'$ on $V$ is $IB=\ker(B\to B/IB)$. The image $\operatorname{im}(g^*\mathcal I_Z\to\mathcal O_{X'})$ is the ideal $\mathcal I_Z\mathcal O_{X'}$ of [def-nagata-extended-ideal]; by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient] (1) (with $f=g$, $\mathcal J=\mathcal I_Z$) it is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals whose sections on $V$ are the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of $I$, that is $IB$. The affine opens $V\subseteq g^{-1}(U)$, for all affine opens $U\subseteq X$, form a basis of $X'$, and both ideals are quasi-coherent ideal sheaves with the same sections $IB$ on each of them, so they are equal [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]: $\mathcal I_{Z'}=\operatorname{im}(g^*\mathcal I_Z\to\mathcal O_{X'})$.

Assume $g$ is flat and use the affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], $B$ is a flat $A$-module. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to the injection $0\to I\to A$: the map $I\otimes_AB\to A\otimes_AB=B$, $a\otimes b\mapsto g^\sharp(a)b$, is injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] (with its naturality applied to $\mathcal I_Z\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_X$, and $\mathcal O_X(U)\otimes_AB=B$), $(g^*\mathcal I_Z)(V)\cong I\otimes_AB$ and the map $(g^*\mathcal I_Z)(V)\to\mathcal O_{X'}(V)=B$ is this map, whose image is $IB=\mathcal I_{Z'}(V)$ by step 1. As these $V$ form a basis of $X'$, the kernel sheaf of $g^*\mathcal I_Z\to\mathcal O_{X'}$ has zero sections on a basis, hence is zero: the map is injective and identifies $g^*\mathcal I_Z$ with the ideal of $Z'$.

proof.text: For $K/k$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat] gives that $K$ is a flat $k$-module, hence $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. The projection $g:X_K\to X$ is its base change along $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, hence flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. The base change of the closed immersion $x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ along $g$ is $x_K:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X_K$ by the universal property of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Apply step 2 to $i=x$ and this $g$.

lead_note: 2026-10-10 L: statement corrected. The blueprint said the ideal sheaf of Z x_X X' is the pullback g^* I_Z; that is false without flatness (D = V(x) in A^1_k and g the inclusion of the origin: g^* I_D = k but I_(D_Y) = 0; found by the worker of lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-properties). Stacks 01JY states only that immersions are stable under base change; the ideal is the image of g^* I_Z -> O_X' (Schemes 01JU (1)); equality holds for flat g. The particular case I_(x_K) = I_x tensor O_(X_K) is a flat base change (field extension). Citers (lem-pc-hilb-functorial, lem-pc-recd-pullback, lem-pc-very-ample-ample, lem-pc-twist, prop-pc-xk-integral, lem-weil-pbc-first-order-thickening-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-thickening-systems-dictionary, lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-properties, lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image) must use the image form or a flat g; checked at their review. 2026-10-10 L: in the final clause the point x : Spec k -> X is a k-morphism (a k-rational point), as the citers use; the reviewer notes the statement does not say so; to be made explicit at the next edit of the statement.

split_report.summary: The blueprint proof incorrectly equated the ideal of every base change with the pulled-back ideal. On affine charts A/I over A and B over A, the base change is Spec(B/IB), so its ideal is the image of I tensor_A B -> B. Flatness of B over A makes this arrow injective. The field-extension case specifies a closed k-rational point and uses flatness of K over k and its base change. All non-elementary inputs are existing Mathlib leaves or definitions, so no node was created.
